title: If the lens has a second radial term the solver does not model, does self-calibrating bundle adjustment still recover the surface?
lede: rendering with k1 = −0.2 and k2 swept from −0.2 to +0.4, a bundle adjustment solving for the focal and k1 only returns 0.0015 object radii, the same as one that also solves k2, against 0.0022–0.0030 with no distortion model; the lens parameters are not separately identified (k1 stays near −0.16, k2 sits about 0.16 low) and the gain vanishes by 2 px noise. Synthetic only
summary: Follows sensing-bafocal, whose fitted radial law was the rendering law, and takes its “model mismatch” next step. Images are rendered on the sensing-ba rig (12 views, 0.5 px noise, every pose wrong) with xd = x(1 + k1r² + k2r⁴). With k1 = −0.2 and k2 from −0.2 to +0.4, an adjustment with no distortion model costs 0.0024–0.0030 (focal free) and 0.0022–0.0027 (focal held), while fitting the focal and k1 alone gives 0.0015 in every case, equal to fitting k2 as well. The parameters are not recovered separately: the k1 estimate is −0.158 whatever the true k2 and the k2 estimate moves with the truth but sits about 0.16 below it, and the focal ends 1.1% off; surface error is insensitive to this. The benefit disappears by 2 px of noise (0.0061 for all three), and at 6 views the focal is 4% off. Limits: synthetic, the lens-parameter ranges are swept, not measured from a device; one object; correct matches; 6 seeds per cell; what the one-term model gets right is the surface, not the lens parameters.
